After mining operations have ceased and reclamation has been completed, it is expected that the only impact on the air quality resulting from previous operations will be some particulate loading from wind erosion effects on roadways and similar areas used for vehicular activity.
At the high-level development production rate it would be necessary to construct mining facilities on Tract II that would encompass about 300 acres. Also, a railroad spur and loop, covering about 212 acres, would be built from the present spur on Tract III across Sarpy Creek to Tract II. This would require the development of approximately 75 more acres of land than to construct the haul road that is included in Scenario I. Therefore, an increase of about 50 percent in the dust loading associated with the development of the coal transporting system could be expected with Scenario II as compared to Scenario I. During these construction activities it is expected that dust emissions will occur at a rate of about one to two tons/acre/month. There would likewise be proportionate increases in heavy-duty construction vehicle emissions and dust loading from travel on unpaved roads with this scenario of coal development as compared to Scenario I.
All other impacts, which are primarily related to dust loading, are expected to have very similar sources and effects as described in Scenario I. Again, the relative total emissions should increase proportionally with the amount of coal production. For example, annual production rates will remain about the same on Tract III regardless of the level of development (Scenario I or Scenario II); however, production should increase by about 100 percent on Tract II under high-level development
